title: Rocket strike on football pitch in Majdal Shams kills children in the Golan Heights
body:
On Saturday 27 July 2024 a rocket struck a football pitch in Majdal Shams, an Israeli-controlled town in the Golan Heights, killing at least 12 people, most of them children and teenagers aged roughly 10 to 20, according to NBC News. A caption on the report cited Magen David Adom, Israel's emergency service, as saying at least nine were killed and 34 wounded at an early stage, 17 of them critically, and emergency services said another 18 young people were wounded.

The Israeli military blamed Hezbollah. Spokesman Daniel Hagari said evidence showed that an Iranian-made Falaq-1 rocket "owned exclusively by Hezbollah" hit the field, and US Secretary of State Antony Blinken said there was "every indication" the rocket came from Hezbollah. Hezbollah denied responsibility, though it claimed attacks on nearby Israeli military targets in the Golan Heights that day. NBC noted that Hezbollah's stated firing time of 5:20 p.m. did not match the Israeli-reported impact time of 6:18 p.m.

On Sunday 28 July the Israel Defense Forces said they struck seven targets deep inside Lebanon, reaching as far as the Bekaa Valley. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut short his trip to the United States, vowed retaliation and said Hezbollah would pay a heavy price. Israel's killing of Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr in Beirut on 30 July was described by Israeli officials as a response to the Majdal Shams strike.
